title: NBA2 site-improvement queue
source_note: Nothing here has been implemented. Each item is written so it can be accepted, rejected or deferred on its own merits, and the Status column is the record of that decision — not of this session's opinion. Ordered by decision-quality gain per unit of effort.

status_key.applied in this PR: already built as part of the integration work
status_key.rejected by design: considered and deliberately not done, with reason

suggestions.title: Connect a licensed odds feed before anything else
suggestions.problem: Without prices there is no edge, no CLV, no ROI and no way to know whether our line is good; the site can only publish projections and triggers.
suggestions.proposal: Add `nba2/ingest/odds.py` writing dated snapshots to data/raw with book, market, line, price and timestamp; keep closing prices permanently.
suggestions.benefit: Unblocks gates G-02, G-05 on real PnL, G-09, and converts every table from 'projection' to 'decision'.
suggestions.risk: Vendor cost; storing closing lines needs storage rights (Q-18 style check).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept first; nothing else on this list pays as well.

suggestions.title: Ingest official game-level results daily
suggestions.problem: σ, HCA, margin/total correlation, prop rates and every backtest all wait on game-level results; today they are fitted from a standings table instead.
suggestions.proposal: Nightly snapshot of final scores by official game ID into data/raw; extend to ≥2 seasons for fitting.
suggestions.benefit: Turns the two fitted constants into measured ones and kills the circularity in G-04.
suggestions.risk: Needs network access from a runner (unavailable in this sandbox).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept with S-01 in the same sprint.

suggestions.title: Store point-in-time snapshots, not 'latest' tables
suggestions.problem: An as-of standings table contains future information for games early in its window, which silently inflates any backtest (G-07 currently AT-RISK for exactly this).
suggestions.proposal: Key every snapshot by (as_of_date, game_date) and make the model read only rows with as_of < tip-off.
suggestions.benefit: Makes historical results believable at all; the single most common way a betting model dies.
suggestions.risk: Storage growth; mitigation: parquet or compressed CSV in a data branch.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept before any backtest is quoted on the site.

suggestions.title: Ratify thresholds in one sitting
suggestions.problem: Eleven numbers decide which games are actionable and who wins the leaderboard, and all eleven are currently mine.
suggestions.proposal: Owner reviews the Parameters page and signs off (or edits) in a single commit; status flips from 'unratified' to 'ratified' in config.
suggestions.benefit: Makes accountability real instead of implied; a one-hour task that removes a whole class of silent bias.
suggestions.risk: None.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept now — it blocks 'is this site trustworthy' more than any data purchase.

suggestions.title: Preregister strategy trials with a counter
suggestions.problem: G-06 (multiple-testing control) is unpayable while nobody records how many variants were tried; the Deflated Sharpe needs N.
suggestions.proposal: Append every evaluation attempt (id, config hash, timestamp, seed) to data/trials.jsonl; leaderboard reads N from it.
suggestions.benefit: Makes the leaderboard a science instead of a search result; costs ~20 lines.
suggestions.risk: Requires discipline to log failed attempts too — that is the point.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept; pair with a rule 'no evaluation without registration'.

suggestions.title: Render 'why is this blank' on every empty cell
suggestions.problem: A blank cell reads as 'no data' but not as 'which missing input, and what would fill it'.
suggestions.proposal: The generator already attaches flag ids to blanks (see the strict rule in nba2/provenance.py::make_row): render the flag id as a tooltip on each blank cell, linking to its entry on the Flagged page.
suggestions.benefit: Turns every gap into a one-click work item for the reviewer instead of a mystery.
suggestions.risk: Adds ~40 lines of build logic; must stay in sync with the flag registry.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept — cheap and it is what the Flagged page exists for.

suggestions.title: Staleness banner with an explicit expiry
suggestions.problem: Lines published from a 3-day-old snapshot look identical to fresh ones; nothing on the page says 'stop'.
suggestions.proposal: Header banner computing age of snapshot vs a policy max age (e.g. 24h), turning red past expiry and disabling the picks tab.
suggestions.benefit: Prevents the most expensive realistic failure: betting yesterday's number today.
suggestions.risk: Needs the scheduled rebuild (S-16) to be meaningful.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept with S-16.

suggestions.title: Replace third-party ratings with an official snapshot
suggestions.problem: Every line currently derives from Basketball-Reference values (PS/G, PA/G, SRS) because the official endpoint was unreachable here; that is flagged (FLAG-RAT-01) but it is the load-bearing wall.
suggestions.proposal: When R-104 is possible, ingest official team stats at a fixed daily time and delete the third-party file; keep both during a parallel period to measure drift.
suggestions.benefit: Removes the largest single caveat on the site and satisfies the 'official source' rule literally.
suggestions.risk: Official endpoint access/licensing (see Q-18's twin problem).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept after S-02.

suggestions.title: Structured injury-PDF parser instead of text extraction
suggestions.problem: 17 of 91 rows needed team attribution from block continuation because the PDF table breaks across pages (FLAG-INJ-01).
suggestions.proposal: Parse the report with a table-aware reader keyed on the Game Date column, and store page/row coordinates for each record.
suggestions.benefit: Kills the attribution caveat and lets the site assert completeness ('all 7 pages parsed').
suggestions.risk: PDF layout changes without notice mid-season.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept; it is a correctness fix, not polish.

suggestions.title: Add a game-day re-issue build (T-0) alongside the T-3 build
suggestions.problem: Injury reports for future days are 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' — proven this session — so a 3-day-ahead line is structurally injury-blind.
suggestions.proposal: Publish two sealed snapshots per day (T-3 and T-0 after the 13:00 ET report) and show the delta between them as the injury signal.
suggestions.benefit: Converts a weakness into a measurable quantity: how much our line moves on availability news, which is a strategy family of its own.
suggestions.risk: Doubles storage of sealed ledgers (small).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept — the best idea on this list for model quality per unit of data.

suggestions.title: Show per-line contribution of every input
suggestions.problem: 'San Antonio -4.5' is opaque: nobody can see how much is rating gap, shrinkage, HCA or injury-blindness.
suggestions.proposal: Add a decomposition column (SRS gap ×λ, raw-margin gap ×λ, HCA, injury adj) per line, computed not asserted.
suggestions.benefit: Reviewers can disagree with a component instead of the whole number; that is how a model gets better.
suggestions.risk: Wider tables on mobile.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept.

suggestions.title: Bankroll/staking page with the actual policy applied
suggestions.problem: Stakes are pinned to 0% by rule until prices exist, which is correct but explains nothing to a reviewer.
suggestions.proposal: A page showing the staking maths with the current caps and what a bet would look like at each available price once S-01 lands.
suggestions.benefit: Makes the 0% legible as a policy rather than a gap.
suggestions.risk: Must not become a calculator that implies a recommendation.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept with a disclaimer requirement.

suggestions.title: Per-game chart: rating gap vs line, with the disagreement band
suggestions.problem: Tables answer 'what number' but not 'how near the decision boundary is this game'.
suggestions.proposal: Small multiples drawn client-side from site.json; the band is the sensitivity box, so a narrow bar = fragile line.
suggestions.benefit: Fragile picks become visible without reading the stability column.
suggestions.risk: Chart code must render the same numbers as the table or we get two truths; generate from the same JSON.
suggestions.recommendation: Defer until S-01/S-02 so there is something worth drawing.

suggestions.title: Table ergonomics: sticky headers, density toggle, CSV export
suggestions.problem: The 31-row lines table and 91-row injury table are the working surface; today they scroll freely and cannot be exported.
suggestions.proposal: Sticky thead, a compact-density class, and a per-table 'download CSV' that includes the source column.
suggestions.benefit: Reviewers can work offline without losing provenance — export keeps the source link per row.
suggestions.risk: None material.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept.

suggestions.title: Accessibility and print path
suggestions.problem: A dense analytical dashboard with no ARIA table semantics and no print stylesheet is hard to review with colleagues.
suggestions.proposal: scope=headers, caption elements, focus styles, and a print stylesheet that keeps source URLs.
suggestions.benefit: Reviewable in a meeting, which is where decisions actually happen.
suggestions.risk: None.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept.

suggestions.title: Scheduled rebuild with a freshness gate
suggestions.problem: The site updates only when a session commits; the numbers are a frozen 2026-11-13 snapshot.
suggestions.proposal: Daily Actions workflow that re-ingests, rebuilds, re-seals, and fails (not publishes) if any official source is unreachable.
suggestions.benefit: Ends the 'is this current?' question. Failure to fetch becomes visible instead of silent staleness.
suggestions.risk: Runner needs network to the official endpoints; a failing schedule must not publish a stale site.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept once S-02 exists.

suggestions.title: Compliance framing on the front page
suggestions.problem: A public page that prints spreads, parlays and staking language reads as betting advice; today the notice is a footer line.
suggestions.proposal: Front-page notice: research tool, no guarantees, 21+/jurisdiction responsibility, links to problem-gambling help.
suggestions.benefit: Reduces real-world harm and the risk of the site being read as a tipster service.
suggestions.risk: None.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept.

suggestions.title: Keep the sealed ledger in git, not a database
suggestions.problem: A leaderboard is only credible if predictions cannot be edited after the fact.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the current design: canonical JSON + sha256, committed with the site build; never rewrite history.
suggestions.benefit: Auditable by anyone with the repo, with no infrastructure to trust.
suggestions.risk: Git history bloat over a season; mitigate with monthly squash archives.
suggestions.recommendation: Already applied; keep unless a DB is required for scale.

suggestions.title: Publish from a build directory instead of the repository root
suggestions.problem: `path: '.'` makes every committed file public, including data snapshots and anything a future session commits by mistake.
suggestions.proposal: Build to `site/` (HTML + assets + data/site.json) and publish that directory only.
suggestions.benefit: Reduces accidental disclosure; keeps the public surface explicit.
suggestions.effort: M (changes every relative link + breaks current live URLs unless redirected)
suggestions.risk: URL churn; needs a redirect plan for the already-live root pages.
suggestions.recommendation: Defer — real improvement, but it breaks existing links and none of the currently committed files are sensitive.

suggestions.title: Stop writing narrative into empty analysis columns
suggestions.problem: The temptation this site is built to resist: a 'game flow' page with adjectives where pace numbers should be.
suggestions.proposal: Keep policy as code (blank + flag is the only permitted empty state) and add a lint rule that fails any prose-only analysis column.
suggestions.benefit: The property that makes everything else on the site usable as evidence.
suggestions.risk: None.
suggestions.recommendation: Already applied via make_row + lint; do not weaken it under time pressure.

suggestions.title: Ship a 'Live verification' page that re-grades the site against today's official pages
suggestions.problem: The site could only claim freshness by asserting it. Nothing on it re-reads an official page at render time, so a stale record and a correct record looked identical (proof: 18 of 30 team records are stale right now while the page still shows MATCH).
suggestions.proposal: A dedicated page, generated from audit/<date>/ captures, that lists each official page read today, what it proved or contradicted, and every published row that no longer matches. Each row links the official URL it was checked against.
suggestions.benefit: Turns 'verified' from a claim into an artefact a reader can audit in ten seconds, and makes staleness visible instead of silent.
suggestions.risk: Needs a disciplined capture ritual; a page built from an old capture is worse than none, so the page prints the fetch timestamp on every row.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept. This is the highest decision-quality gain per unit of effort on the site.

suggestions.title: Publish the true sample size next to every hit rate, never the inflated one
suggestions.problem: The graded picks read as 8-0. They are 4-0: four games were each bet by two strategies, so a reader scanning the strategy tables sees double the evidence that exists.
suggestions.proposal: Every hit-rate table carries both numbers - 'signal rows graded' and 'distinct games' - and any strategy with fewer than the ratified minimum shows 'insufficient evidence' in place of a ranking.
suggestions.benefit: Removes the single most common way a small sample is made to look like skill.
suggestions.risk: None; it can only reduce claims.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept and make it a lint rule: a hit rate without its n cannot render.

suggestions.title: Score the model against named naive baselines before it scores itself
suggestions.problem: The site reports model accuracy without the baselines that would beat it. On the nine graded games the model's winner accuracy (5/9) equals a net-rating baseline (5/9) and loses to 'always pick home' (7/9).
suggestions.proposal: Every accuracy number renders beside three free baselines computed from the same frozen inputs: home always, higher net rating, higher SRS. A strategy cannot be ranked above the best baseline it fails to beat.
suggestions.benefit: Kills the 'my model is 56%' claim that a coin plus home-court advantage already produces.
suggestions.risk: On small n the baseline will sometimes win by luck - which is the point, and the page says so.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept; make 'beats the best baseline at p<0.05' a gate condition rather than a comment.

suggestions.title: Make the suggestions page an explicit decision queue with owner actions
suggestions.problem: Suggestions were a list of proposals with a status string. A reviewer could not accept, reject or defer one in a way that changed anything, so the queue's state was decorative.
suggestions.proposal: Each suggestion renders with four fields: evidence (a live source link), what changes if accepted, effort, and an owner action of accept / reject / defer. The page states plainly that nothing has been implemented on the owner's behalf and that accept is the only state that authorises work.
suggestions.benefit: The owner can choose a path before any of it is built, which is exactly what the brief asks for.
suggestions.risk: None; it is a presentation contract.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept.

suggestions.title: Add a staleness gate to the build, not just a timestamp to the page
suggestions.problem: Every page prints an as-of date, but no build fails when the date is old. The stamp is honest and inert.
suggestions.proposal: nba2/v2/check.py fails when a table's newest capture is older than a per-table limit (records 24h, injuries to the next filing, prices 15m), and the Pages workflow cannot publish a build that fails it.
suggestions.benefit: Makes 'up to date' enforceable, which is the only way it survives contact with a busy week.
suggestions.risk: A stale official source would block deploys; mitigated by letting the gate downgrade to a loud banner after N hours rather than a hard fail on the whole site.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept, after Q-23 is answered (the limits are the owner's risk appetite, not mine).

suggestions.title: Fix the spread-sign inversion in the S2 selections before any of it is graded by a human
suggestions.problem: S2_SpreadValue emits 'POR +6.0' for a game where the same file's label says 'POR -6.0' and the model has POR as a 6.07-point favourite. A reader taking that at face value takes the wrong side of the model's own number.
suggestions.proposal: Correct the away-side sign in nba2/picks.py so a selection always names the side with the points. Regenerate picks.json. Do not touch data/raw/ledger (the sealed ledgers are immutable).
suggestions.benefit: Removes a defect that silently inverts a published recommendation.
suggestions.risk: picks.json is another session's artefact; the change is logged here for its owner rather than made unilaterally.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept and assign to the owner of nba2/picks.py.

suggestions.title: Retire the unreachable v1 tree instead of maintaining two generators
suggestions.problem: Probed on 2026-11-14: exactly one tree is published (site/). The root v1 tree returns 404 for every page — pages/session-audit.html and pages/executive-summary.html were both checked — yet ci.yml still regenerates, lints and parity-checks it on every push, and it carries records that are stale since the 11/13 finals.
suggestions.proposal: Move root index.html, pages/**, flagged.html and data/site.json under archive/ with a dated note explaining what each was, drop the v1 parity step from ci.yml, and delete nothing.
suggestions.benefit: One number per question is the precondition for every other claim on the site.
suggestions.risk: Breaks inbound links to the old trees; the redirect pages fix that.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept, as the first integration action (this is Q-27).

suggestions.title: Run the test suite against a fresh clone before trusting 'committed == rebuilt'
suggestions.problem: The v1 determinism test passed on every working copy and failed on every clean clone, because two published values depended on the presence of a previous build. Local runs rewrote the artefact and then compared it with itself.
suggestions.proposal: Add a CI job that clones the repository into a temp directory, runs the suite there, then rebuilds and asserts a clean git status. The publish-parity workflow now does the rebuild half; the clone half is the part that caught this.
suggestions.benefit: Turns a class of silent, self-erasing test passes into a failure at PR time.
suggestions.risk: Adds ~30s of CI; no production risk.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept — this is the check that found F-029.
